Policy Name: Cigna Lumbar Fusion (CMM-609: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression)
Referred Sections: CMM-609.7: Lumbar Fusion (with or without Decompression) Following Failed Lumbar Disc Arthroplasty Surgery

Required findings: Post‑operative imaging (plain radiograph, CT or MRI) demonstrates implant malposition, subsidence, loosening, infection, dislocation, subluxation, vertebral body fracture, or dislodgement
Patient reports persistent or worsening back pain and/or radicular symptoms attributable to the failed implant
Conservative management (physical therapy, activity modification, analgesics) attempted for ≥6 weeks without adequate relief
Patient is nicotine‑free verified by serum, saliva, or urine cotinine test within 30 days of surgery
No uncontrolled psychiatric or behavioral health disorder that would impair postoperative recovery
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.7 > Failed Lumbar Disc Arthroplasty Implant

Required findings: ≥6 months elapsed since the index lumbar disc arthroplasty at the same level
Post‑operative MRI or CT shows neural element compression (retained disc material, recurrent herniation, or osteophyte) correlating with symptoms
Objective neurologic deficits on exam (e.g., motor weakness, sensory loss, reflex changes) consistent with imaging
Documented failure of ≥6 weeks of guideline‑based conservative therapy (PT, NSAIDs/analgesics, epidural steroid injection)
Nicotine abstinence confirmed by cotinine testing and no active substance abuse
Behavioral health assessment completed with no uncontrolled condition
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.7 > Evidence of Neural Structure Compression

Non-Indications: Lumbar fusion performed <6 months after the original disc arthroplasty
Absence of implant failure or radiographic neural compression
No documented neurologic deficit or concordant imaging findings
Failure to complete the required trial of conservative therapy
Active tobacco use without documented cessation and negative cotinine test
Uncontrolled psychiatric or behavioral health disorder
Procedure performed without meeting the specific criteria in CMM-609.4 (fusion with decompression) or CMM-609.5 (fusion without decompression)
Important criteria & exceptions: Cotinine testing may be serum (cut‑off 3‑20 ng/mL), saliva (10‑44 ng/mL), or urine (≤10 ng/mL) and must be performed within 30 days of the planned surgery
If the patient cannot tolerate a full 6‑week conservative trial due to severe disability, a documented justification from the treating surgeon may be accepted
When both implant failure and neural compression are present, either indication satisfies the requirement; only one set of full criteria needs to be met
Maximum of one lumbar level fusion per episode unless multi‑level instability is documented in the operative report
Documentation required: Operative report of the original lumbar disc arthroplasty including level(s) and implant details
Post‑operative plain radiographs, CT or MRI report demonstrating implant malposition/failure or neural compression
Neurologic examination note documenting deficits (strength, sensation, reflexes)
Physical therapy and/or pain management records showing ≥6 weeks of conservative therapy
Medication list and pharmacy records for analgesics/NSAIDs used during conservative phase
Cotinine test result (serum, saliva, or urine) with date and value
Behavioral health evaluation note confirming stability or treatment plan
Surgeon’s clinical note summarizing indication (implant failure vs. neural compression) and confirming time interval >6 months
